units.translation: ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ are also later the chief means of proof, and these are called here according to the manuscripts ⟦3⟧ (after 786, 379 (⟦4⟧). ⟦5⟧. For otherwise not), in that they take the place of the old oaths of the parties and are better and more reliable than these; cf. ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧ (scil. ⟦8⟧). The scholiast also read thus (⟦9⟧, admittedly quite wrongly), and we need not change with Pauw to ⟦10⟧ (an unattested word). Nor is the ⟦11⟧ after ⟦12⟧ (Wellauer) necessary, cf. on ⟦13⟧ ⟦14⟧ ⟦15⟧, ⟦16⟧ ⟦17⟧ etc., Kühner-Gerth 1, 371.
the Pythian pledges, the well-sworn oaths
but you, demand oaths from them
⟦1⟧ middle voice as at ⟦2⟧. 216. ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ is a zeugma.

V. 487 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧; so also elsewhere Aeschylus ⟦3⟧ -⟦4⟧, except ⟦5⟧ Ag. For the neuter Wecklein compares ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧ is ⟦8⟧ an easy change by Auratus (for which Heimsoeth compares the scholium on 556 ⟦9⟧); ⟦10⟧ Schneidewin, which is also not difficult; but one can also attach the infinitive to ⟦11⟧vada.
Athena leads those who will judge
I will come to these things

V. 489 is ⟦1⟧ an emendation supported by the scholium (⟦2⟧); but ⟦3⟧ (Markland) has the difficulty (Paley) that ⟦4⟧ "to indicate" does not suit a judicial verdict. So better Schütz ⟦5⟧, with a comma after ⟦6⟧, = ⟦7⟧, which was the formula in the Attic heliastic oath, ⟦8⟧ etc., for cases where (as here) no opposition provided the norm for the decision. Cf. (⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧) 1143 ⟦11⟧, ⟦12⟧ ⟦13⟧, 750. ⟦14⟧ etc.; further for ⟦15⟧ (⟦16⟧) as a strong negation before an adjective 730 ⟦17⟧ . . ⟦18⟧, ⟦19⟧. 833. With this Athena departs into the city, and with her probably also Orestes, who is assumed as ⟦20⟧ (the scholiast thinks otherwise); cf. ⟦21⟧. 506 and ⟦22⟧ 486, although the Erinyes in fact have no reason to go anywhere for this, and the continuation of the play requires their presence in the theater. The scene changes during the choral song to the Areopagus, see on 566.
